properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD: NO `cancelled` VALUE IS ADDED TO `Capability.status`, NOW OR LATER.** Abandonment is recorded by an accepted Decision drawing `OBSOLETES`, which computes `discontinued`. The question this node was opened under is answered; what remains is a measurement and a separate, narrower question, both named below.

⭐ **AND THE DETECTOR IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT YET — THAT IS THE PART OF THE RULING WORTH KEEPING.** Three ways to make an agent find `OBSOLETES` were on the table: a hint on `set_capability_status`, a DETECTOR for abandonment words in description prose, and the command coverage. **The vocabulary fix shipped in v0.31.0** (`Capability.status` and the `OBSOLETES` hint now name each other, pinned by tests) **and has never been in front of an agent** — Alex's fleet has not seen it. Building the detector now would be guessing that the cheap fix failed before observing whether it did, and it is the only option with a false-positive cost: a capability legitimately describing that it REPLACED something dropped would fire.

🎯 **WHAT IS OWED IS THEREFORE A MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS FREE.** Alex's fleet is the only place "DROPPED in prose" was ever observed. **If it stops appearing there after v0.31.0, the vocabulary fix worked and the detector is unnecessary; if it continues, the detector is justified by evidence rather than by fear.** Same discipline Anthony applied to the allocation question — do not reason about it, measure it.

⚠️ **THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND BELONGS ELSEWHERE, NOT HERE:** a capability **nobody ever agreed to** has no decision to hang an `OBSOLETES` edge from, so neither this ruling nor the 2026-08-11 one reaches it. That is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s, and closing this node does not close that.

════════ THE REASONING THAT PRODUCED THE RULING ════════

🛑 **ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, CHALLENGING THE PREMISE: "we already have an obsolete with discontinued or something like that — are we playing semantics with cancelled?" CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE AND THE GRAPH RATHER THAN ARGUED. HE IS RIGHT FOR THE ABANDONED CASE, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY DECIDED THREE DAYS EARLIER.**

`dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` was **DECIDED on his word 2026-08-11**: a Decision `OBSOLETES` what it withdrew, the decision itself being the source. No enum value, no edge type, no schema stamp move, no upgrade doc.

**IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — IT IS LIVE IN THIS GRAPH.** `dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued` (accepted) obsoletes `cap:content-store` and `cap:content-manifest` (both stored `realized`) and `cap:session-artifacts` (`verified`). And `is_discontinued` has FOUR readers: `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability` and `unverified_capability` fall silent, and delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier (`DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued`).

⇒ **ADDING `cancelled` WOULD BE A SECOND WAY TO SAY WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY COMPUTES — and worse than redundant, because a STORED status can disagree with the COMPUTED one.** The stored status deliberately keeps saying what was BUILT; that is why `get_node` carries `discontinued` separately and warns to read it.

═══ ⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY BIT ALEX IS DISCOVERABILITY, NOT A MISSING STATE ═══

His agents typed "DROPPED" into description prose while the mechanism existed and worked. Measured via `describe_schema`, which the served routing table tells an agent to use for exactly this lookup: `Capability.status` carried **no description at all** — four bare values and no fifth — while every neighbouring property carried a teaching one; and `OBSOLETES`'s entire hint read *"Source makes target redundant or deprecated"*, naming neither the retirement job, nor the Decision as source, nor `discontinued`. **So an agent did everything right and still had nowhere to put the fact except prose.** Both descriptions shipped in v0.31.0, with no schema stamp move.

════════ THE ORIGINAL REPORT, KEPT ════════

Alex's fleet, 2026-08-09: 'Requirements: deferred / dropped. Capabilities: no equivalent — agents stuff DROPPED into description text.' CONFIRMED AGAINST THE SCHEMA: Requirement.status is [proposed, accepted, deferred, dropped, met]; Capability.status is [planned, in_progress, realized, verified]. WHY IT IS THE WEEK'S OWN DEFECT CLASS AGAIN: a state that cannot be expressed does not disappear — it gets smuggled into prose.
properties.name: DECIDED — no cancelled state, ever: abandonment is an OBSOLETES edge, and whether the vocabulary fix was enough is a MEASUREMENT owed by Alex's fleet, not a further decision
properties.rationale: Raised by a second consumer project rather than found here, which is the useful part: reflow2's own graph never hit it because this project retires capabilities rather than cancelling them. Kept as a decision point rather than built because it is a schema enum change that would move the stamp and therefore owe an upgrade doc — the first this week that would — and because it touches an already-open question about retirement being modelled in two places. Anthony's to settle.
